subject: Fixing Error variance with ordered categorical data

messages.author: 1bf7e33a92c33ed5
messages.subject: Fixing Error variance with ordered categorical data
parts:
When estimating a model with categorical (ordered) variables- and WLSMV estimation method -, I obtain a negative error variance. How can I set the variance to a value close to 0 using theta parameterization method?
Thanks in advance

messages.subject: Re: Fixing Error variance with ordered categorical data

fittedmodel <- lavaan(yourmodel, data = your.data, ordered = your.ordinal.items, parameterization = "theta", mimic = "mplus",auto.th = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fixing Error variance with ordered categorical data
parts: in lavaan WLSMV estimator by default use the delta parameterization method, and I believe that this method does not allow setting a negative error variance to a value close to zero
Correct, error variances are not model parameters under delta parameterization.  They are merely implied by the latent scales and the explained variance.
My question is: how can I estimate in lavaan a model using the WLSMV estimator with  theta parameterization?

If your error variance is negative under delta, I would guess your model would fail to converge under theta parameterization, because that variance would be fixed to 1 for identification.

The issue is not the negative variance; that is just one side of a two-sided coin.  The explained variance exceeds 1, which is what the delta parameterization assumes the total variance is.  Fixing that variance to zero would not solve the "problem" anyway, only mask it, and in so doing, create other problems.

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/1082-989X.13.2.150

If you only have 1 predictor, all explained variance is due to a single parameter, so you could check the CI around its standardized value to test whether its population value < 1 (which would imply the population error variance > 0).

https://doi.org/10.1177%2F0049124112442138

For example, if this is an indicator in a CFA, you could use std.lv=TRUE to fix factor variances to 1, in which case loadings under the delta parameterization are already standardized parameters.  So you could request summary(fit, ci = TRUE)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
